boundary_rationale: “Then Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Jer.16.1), rendering vayehi debar-YHWH וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.16.1, byte tier) -- one of the book's narrative word-event onsets. The command that follows, “You shall not take a wife” (web:Jer.16.2), opens on לֹֽא תִקַּ֥ח לְךָ֖ אִשָּׁ֑ה (oshb:Jer.16.2, byte tier), its own koh-amar rationale running from 16:3 through 16:4. A second command in the same voice follows without a scene change: “Don't enter into the house of mourning” (web:Jer.16.5) carries its koh-amar formula in the same verse as the prohibition itself, כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל תָּבוֹא֙ בֵּ֣ית מַרְזֵ֔חַ (oshb:Jer.16.5, byte tier), with 16:6-7 running on as that command's rationale and carrying no formula of its own. A third command, “You shall not go into the house of feasting” (web:Jer.16.8), closes with the full divine-name stack “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says”, כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.16.9, byte tier). The three prohibitions stay one row because the second-person-singular addressee of the commands at 16:2, 16:5 and 16:8 never changes; the second-person-plural at לְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם וּבִֽימֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.16.9, byte tier) sits inside the quoted oracle content, addressing the people the oracle describes rather than marking a fresh frame addressee, and each koh-amar onset explains the command just given rather than opening a new frame-owner.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 16:1-9 as a symbolic_act_report alongside the book's other enacted signs was considered and set aside: the span pairs its three prohibitions with their own rationale without narrating Jeremiah's own compliance in a first-person performance clause the way the potter's-house sign that opens the next frame does (web:Jer.18.3), so the material was kept in command-and-rationale form as judgment_oracle.

boundary_rationale: “The word which came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying” (web:Jer.18.1) opens הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.18.1, byte tier) -- the hadavar-asher-hayah-el-Yirmeyahu shape that opens this frame. The command “Arise, and go down to the potter’s house” (web:Jer.18.2), ק֥וּם וְיָרַדְתָּ֖ בֵּ֣ית הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר וְשָׁ֖מָּה אַשְׁמִֽיעֲךָ֥ אֶת דְּבָרָֽי (oshb:Jer.18.2, byte tier), and the performance “Then I went down to the potter’s house” (web:Jer.18.3), וָאֵרֵ֖ד בֵּ֣ית הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר (oshb:Jer.18.3, byte tier; the same verse carries a ketiv/qere note on its own 'behold' clause just after, consulted and not spliced through), lead into a second, internal word-event, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֽוֹר (oshb:Jer.18.5, byte tier), and Yahweh's interpretation, “House of Israel, can’t I do with you as this potter?” (web:Jer.18.6), הֲכַיּוֹצֵ֨ר הַזֶּ֜ה לֹא אוּכַ֨ל לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָכֶ֛ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Jer.18.6, byte tier), the same verse closing on the plain article-bearing noun, בְּיַ֣ד הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר (oshb:Jer.18.6, byte tier). The application to Judah by name, “Behold, I frame evil against you” (web:Jer.18.11), turns the same consonantal root into a verb rather than repeating the noun: הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י יוֹצֵ֤ר עֲלֵיכֶם֙ רָעָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier) is a bare participle, byte-distinct from the article-bearing noun that names the craftsman at 18:2, 18:3, 18:4 and 18:6 (sweep: 5 verses on the article-bearing form); the shared object is the consonantal root itself, which recurs at the wider, article-free search across the book (sweep: 10 verses on the bare root). That shared root, not a repeated token, binds the application and the people's own refusal, “It is in vain” (web:Jer.18.12), נוֹאָ֑שׁ (oshb:Jer.18.12, byte tier), to the observed sign. The join that follows changes neither the divine mouth nor, until mid-verse, the addressee: the instruction “Ask now among the nations” (web:Jer.18.13), שַֽׁאֲלוּ נָא֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), repeats the same second-person-plural imperative-plus-entreaty shape already commanding Judah two verses earlier, שׁ֣וּבוּ נָ֗א (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier); its own formula, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), is subordinated to the back-linking לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier) rather than opening a fresh frame -- the identical formula, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier), already stands inside the command to speak at 18:11, so the same mouth carries both sides of the join.
